why: P2 because it closes a real gap between stated intent (networkactive=0) and actual behavior: mapport and Tor control kept probing/connecting in the background despite the user disabling networking
Matters for privacy- and resource-conscious operators (e.g. Tor users) who rely on networkactive=0 to mean no network activity, verified with real packet capture by brunoerg

result.summary: This PR wires NAT-PMP port mapping and the Tor control connection into CConnman::SetNetworkActive so both subsystems start and stop dynamically with the node's network-active state, including via the setnetworkactive RPC at runtime, not just at startup. It supersedes an earlier alternative (#34467) that only gated these subsystems at init time. Two functional tests are added covering mapport and torcontrol behavior under networkactive toggling, plus a Tor reconnect-backoff test.
result.problem: When -networkactive=0 is set, bitcoind still performs NAT-PMP gateway queries and Tor control connection attempts in the background, contradicting the documented meaning of the flag (issue #34190). This affects any operator who expects the flag to fully suspend outbound network activity, including privacy-conscious Tor users.

open_concerns: winterrdog (2026-08-18): a rapid off/on toggle of networkactive during a Tor reconnect backoff sleep can leave the backoff timer growing instead of resetting, with a reproduction test and a proposed diff; not yet addressed by the author

brunoerg earlier noted functional tests can't easily hit the disconnect-guard code path in torcontrol.cpp; author explained this is a defensive check and accepted brunoerg's suggested additional coverage

winterrdog's earlier question about a redundant network-active check in the loop was acknowledged by the author as redundant but harmless
